classification.classification_note: The immediate fault is an 8-byte read of a missing PKCS#11 3.0 function pointer from the global `mock_module_no_slots` table after `base_C_MessageEncryptInit()` treats that legacy `CK_FUNCTION_LIST` object as a `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0`.

bug_description.original:
Project: p11-kit
Crash Type: Global-buffer-overflow READ 8
Crash State:
  base_C_MessageEncryptInit
  rpc_C_MessageEncryptInit
  p11_rpc_server_handle
Sanitizer: address
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` in `base_C_MessageEncryptInit()` on the exact vulnerable commit `7fe7e5d95d9197e7f52aab314468d424acc6ac88`. The staged 27-byte p11-kit RPC blob is parsed as a `C_MessageEncryptInit` request with signature `"uMu"`, so `rpc_C_MessageEncryptInit()` forwards into the PKCS#11 3.0 adapter `base_C_MessageEncryptInit()`. That adapter aliases `virt->lower_module` as `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0 *`, but the fuzz harness bound `virt->lower_module` to `mock_module_no_slots`, which is only a `CK_FUNCTION_LIST` global. Vulnerable `common/mock.c` still initializes that legacy table's version field to `{ CRYPTOKI_VERSION_MAJOR, CRYPTOKI_VERSION_MINOR } = {3,0}`, so the `if (funcs->version.major < 3)` gate does not reject the 3.0 entrypoint and the next statement reads `funcs->C_MessageEncryptInit` as the fifth PKCS#11 3.0 member. Because `mock_module_no_slots` ends at `C_WaitForSlotEvent`, that function-pointer load occurs 32 bytes past the 552-byte global, exactly matching the saved ASan report. The fixing patch changes legacy mock tables back to version 2.40 and adds separate `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0` tables, so the version gate no longer authorizes 3.0-member access on the undersized object.

source.description: First project parser step that materializes the attacker-controlled RPC selector used by the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged 27-byte `poc` begins `00 00 00 44 00 00 00 03 75 4D 75 ...`; this statement reads the first four bytes as `call_id = 0x44`, and later in the same function lines 202-221 map that value to `msg.call_id = P11_RPC_CALL_C_MessageEncryptInit` and verify the following byte-array field as request signature `"uMu"`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The RPC header bytes first materialize the request selector `call_id`; the following signature check at lines 214-221 confirms that this witness uses the `"uMu"` request layout for the selected `C_MessageEncryptInit` call.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The `mock_module_no_slots` object is declared as the smaller legacy `CK_FUNCTION_LIST`, but its version field advertises PKCS#11 3.0, so virtual 3.0 adapters later trust the object as if the 3.0 tail of function pointers were present.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch changes this initializer to `{ CRYPTOKI_LEGACY_VERSION_MAJOR, CRYPTOKI_LEGACY_VERSION_MINOR }` and introduces a separate `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0 mock_module_v3_no_slots` for real 3.0 entrypoints.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The adapter reads the `C_MessageEncryptInit` function pointer from beyond the end of `mock_module_no_slots` after treating that object as a `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0`.
sink.note: The saved ASan report names this exact line as a `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` and says the address is 32 bytes to the right of global `mock_module_no_slots` defined at `common/mock.c:3877`, whose size is 552 bytes.

parser_admitted.description: After `p11_rpc_message_parse()` accepts the request header, the server switch selects the `C_MessageEncryptInit` RPC arm, so control is already inside the PKCS#11 3.0 message-encryption path that reaches `base_C_MessageEncryptInit()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not add instrumentation.

The staged artifacts fully establish the request header semantics (`call_id = C_MessageEncryptInit`, signature `"uMu"`) and the saved ASan stack proves `rpc_C_MessageEncryptInit()` completed its forwarding call, but the exact `session`, `mechanism`, and `key` body values are not independently reconstructable from the saved artifacts alone. Those values are not consumed before the out-of-bounds function-pointer read at step 6.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness initializes a `p11_virtual` wrapper over `mock_module_no_slots` and passes the raw attacker-controlled RPC blob into `p11_rpc_server_handle()`.
The RPC header is parsed as `C_MessageEncryptInit` with signature `"uMu"`, and the corresponding RPC handler forwards into the virtual `C_MessageEncryptInit` entrypoint.
The virtual adapter aliases the bound lower module as `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0 *`, but the bound object is `mock_module_no_slots`, a legacy `CK_FUNCTION_LIST` global that still advertises version 3.0.
Because the version check sees major version 3, the adapter reads the missing `C_MessageEncryptInit` function pointer 32 bytes past the end of `mock_module_no_slots`, matching the saved ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four bytes of the attacker-controlled RPC blob materialize as `call_id = 0x44`. Later in the same function, `msg.call_id` is set from that value and the next byte-array field is verified as signature `"uMu"`, admitting the `C_MessageEncryptInit` request shape that the RPC switch will use.

Once the parsed `call_id` selects the `C_MessageEncryptInit` arm, the RPC handler completes the `uMu` argument decode and forwards to the virtual `self->C_MessageEncryptInit` function. The parsed `session`, `mechanism`, and `key` values are not dereferenced before the later out-of-bounds function-pointer load.

The PKCS#11 3.0 adapter aliases `virt->lower_module` as a `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0 *`. In the harness, `p11_virtual_init (&base, &p11_virtual_base, &mock_module_no_slots, NULL)` at `fuzz/rpc_fuzzer.c:43` prebound `virt->lower_module` to `&mock_module_no_slots`, so `funcs` now points at that global table.

Root cause. `mock_module_no_slots` is declared as `CK_FUNCTION_LIST`, and its initializer ends at `mock_C_WaitForSlotEvent__no_event`, so the object contains no PKCS#11 3.0 members. Nevertheless line 3878 advertises version `{3,0}`, which makes the alias from step 3 look like a valid `CK_FUNCTION_LIST_3_0` table.

The only guard before the 3.0 access trusts `version.major`. Because step 4 made `mock_module_no_slots.version.major == 3`, this branch is not taken even though `funcs` still points to a legacy `CK_FUNCTION_LIST` object without a `C_MessageEncryptInit` member.

Sink. `C_MessageEncryptInit` is the fifth PKCS#11 3.0 function pointer after `C_WaitForSlotEvent`, so on the undersized `mock_module_no_slots` object this statement reads 8 bytes 32 bytes past the end of the 552-byte global. That is the exact `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` reported by ASan.

format.name: p11-kit PKCS#11 RPC request
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 27-byte big-endian p11-kit RPC request blob preserved in the result directory. Its first four bytes are `00 00 00 44`, so `p11_rpc_message_parse()` materializes `call_id = 0x44` and the server selects the `C_MessageEncryptInit` RPC arm; the next RPC byte-array field is the 3-byte signature `"uMu"`, which admits the MessageEncryptInit request layout. Those exact witness semantics are sufficient for the saved crash because `base_C_MessageEncryptInit()` faults while loading the missing `C_MessageEncryptInit` function pointer from `mock_module_no_slots`, before any lower-module implementation can inspect the parsed `session`, `mechanism`, or `key` values.
